results.crypto: libsecp256k1 0.2.0 (C, system library, via rbsecp256k1 6.0.2; schnorr_sig 1.2.0.1 fast path)
results.notes: nostrb at its documented fastest: the optional gems it lists (Nostrb::Optional::GEMS) installed, rbsecp256k1 6.0.2 (schnorr_sig switches to libsecp256k1, its documented "fast" implementation) and oj 3.17.8 (nostrb.rb uses Oj for parse and for the id serialization when it loads). Otherwise as nostrb-client: SignedEvent.validate! + verify(check_id: true) by the harness, the 99-value tag cap drops one valid event of all. rbsecp256k1 is built against the system libsecp256k1 (libsecp256k1-dev), since its bundled source download is unavailable here. Config: CONSOLE_LEVEL=error (see nostrb-client).

Slow pass: one timed run (no warmup for Dart, JVM and Ruby), in the same batch as the other rows. The client hands the app each text frame as a String (on :message) and does nothing else with it: the app JSON.parses the frame and builds a Nostr::Event, as the README does. Nothing is verified by default; the harness calls Event#verify_signature (signature only) and checks the id with the library's own Nostr::Crypto#hash_event (private; SHA-256 of JSON.dump(event.serialize)). Config: Client.new(logger: nil) (the default ColorLogger prints every frame to the console). verify_signature raises Schnorr::InvalidSignatureError on "sig":"" instead of returning false (counted as rejected). Client has no disconnect: teardown unsubscribes and stops the process-global EventMachine reactor; the next run's connect starts a new one.

Slow pass: one timed run (no warmup for Dart, JVM and Ruby), in the same batch as the other rows. The client parses frames into Nostr::Event (Event.from_message, which checks field types only) but has no verify function at all: it signs with bip-schnorr and never verifies. The harness verifies with the library's own crypto dependency: id = SHA-256 of JSON.dump(event.serialize) (the library's serialize), signature with Schnorr.valid_sig? (bip-schnorr). on(:event) fires for every subscription (the event carries no subscription id). Config: defaults.

Slow pass: one timed run (no warmup for Dart, JVM and Ruby), in the same batch as the other rows. Default configuration (stdlib json, pure-Ruby schnorr_sig; nostrb-fast is the documented fast one). subscribe yields each event as a plain Hash (JSON.parse with the gem's NIP-01 options) and verifies nothing. The harness calls the library's Nostrb::SignedEvent.validate! + SignedEvent.verify(check_id: true) (signature, then id) and drops events that raise (validate! then verify is the order the gem's own Relay uses). validate! caps a tag at 99 values (Nostrb.tags!), so it drops one valid event of the corpus (kind 9734 zap request eff6ff2f..., a 104-value relays tag): accepted_ok is false for that reason. subscribe connects lazily, so the WebSocket handshake is inside the timed part, and EOSE reaches the app when subscribe returns. The gem does not declare its async-websocket dependency (Gemfile adds it). Config: CONSOLE_LEVEL=error silences async-pool's per-connection "Attempt to unlock a mutex which is not locked" warning on close.
